name: Tanzania
summary_text: Tanzania is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. The Penal Code criminalises same-sex activity with up to life imprisonment, and the political environment has been actively hostile since the Magufuli-era crackdowns (arrests, forced anal examinations documented by HRW in earlier years, de-registration of LGBT-serving organisations). The 2024 case of Mauzinde is emblematic: a transgender woman and activist found abandoned in a forest in Rahaleo, beaten, her ears cut off — an attack the UN Human Rights Office called “horrendous.” OONI documented extensive targeted blocking of LGBTQ websites correlating with the escalating crackdown, and Amnesty's 2024 regional report notes Tanzanian pushes to further criminalise LGBT people. Zanzibar has its own, harsher penal code. There is no legal gender recognition and no protection infrastructure. For a visitor: visible trans presentation risks arrest under indecency provisions and mob violence; Zanzibar is worse than the mainland.

sources.title: UN rights office denounces 'horrendous' attack on Tanzania transgender activist - JURIST - News
sources.claim_summary: JURIST (June 2024): the UN Human Rights Office denounced the 'horrendous' attack on Tanzanian trans woman and activist Mauzinde - found abandoned in a forest, beaten, with her ears cut; the UN office said she had been 'tortured & sexually assaulted by 12 men' and called for bold action against discrimination.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Tanzania's criminalisation of same-sex activity (life imprisonment possible).
NOTE: The OONI report on internet censorship in Tanzania (2024) returned no extractable text at fetch time (image-based PDF).

Amnesty International report (Jan 2024) 'We Are Facing Extinction': escalating anti-LGBTI sentiment, the weaponization of law and their human-rights implications in select African countries - country profiles including Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Ghana and others.

sources.title: Interview: The LGBT community in Tanzania – Rainer Ebert
sources.claim_summary: Rainer Ebert interview (Sept 2020): 'The LGBT community in Tanzania' - three Tanzanian activists (a lesbian woman, a trans woman, a gay man, all anonymous) describe substantial prejudice, discrimination and violence and denial of basic rights; published with a Swahili version.

Zanzibar Penal Decree Act No. 6 of 2004 (full text): the criminal code of semiautonomous Zanzibar - includes its sexual-offence provisions criminalising same-sex conduct with penalties up to life imprisonment.

US State Department 2013 Human Rights Report for Tanzania: the three most widespread problems were security-force excessive force, gender-based violence including FGM/C, and lack of access to justice; also 'discrimination based on sexual orientation' and societal violence against persons with albinism.
